content: Prefer TypeScript generic constraints with extends over unbounded type parameters so a function like function pick<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K) narrows correctly at call sites.
summary: Use extends to constrain TS generics

content: Default generic type parameters in TypeScript should only be used when the default is genuinely the common case, e.g. class Cache<T = string>, otherwise callers silently get the wrong type.
summary: When to use default generic type parameters

content: Avoid using any as a generic fallback in TypeScript; use unknown and narrow instead so callers cannot bypass type checking.
summary: Avoid any as a generic fallback

content: TypeScript conditional types like T extends U ? X : Y are useful for mapped utility types but hurt readability past two levels of nesting.
summary: Limit nesting of TS conditional types

content: Generic interfaces in TypeScript should be named with a single capital letter (T, K, V) only when their meaning is obvious from context, otherwise use a descriptive name like TItem.
summary: Naming convention for TS generic parameters

content: Variance issues with TypeScript generics show up most often in callback parameter types; prefer readonly arrays to avoid accidental covariant mutation bugs.
summary: TS generic variance and readonly arrays

content: Utility types like Partial, Pick, and Omit compose better than hand-rolled generic helper types for TypeScript DTOs.
summary: Prefer built-in TS utility types over custom ones

content: Standard procedure for a new Python service: create a virtual environment with python -m venv .venv, activate it, then pip install -r requirements.txt before running anything.
summary: Python venv setup procedure

content: Always pin exact versions in requirements.txt for Python services (package==1.2.3, not package>=1.2.3) so a fresh venv install is reproducible across machines.
summary: Pin exact versions in Python requirements.txt

content: Use pyenv to manage multiple Python interpreter versions on a dev machine instead of relying on the system python3.
summary: Use pyenv for Python version management

content: Never commit a .venv directory to git; add it to .gitignore alongside __pycache__ and *.pyc.
summary: Do not commit .venv to git

content: Prefer pip-tools (pip-compile) over hand-editing requirements.txt so transitive dependency pins are generated, not guessed.
summary: Use pip-tools to generate requirements.txt

content: For Python services with native extensions, document the required system packages (e.g. libpq-dev) in the README, not just requirements.txt.
summary: Document native system deps for Python builds

content: CI should recreate the Python virtual environment from scratch every run rather than caching site-packages, to catch missing pins early.
summary: CI rebuilds Python venv from scratch

content: In Go, wrap errors with fmt.Errorf("doing X: %w", err) so callers can unwrap with errors.Is/errors.As instead of string-matching error messages.
summary: Wrap Go errors with %w for unwrapping

content: Sentinel errors in Go should be package-level vars like var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found"), compared with errors.Is, never with ==.
summary: Go sentinel errors and errors.Is

content: Do not use panic/recover for ordinary error handling in Go; reserve panic for truly unrecoverable programmer errors.
summary: Reserve Go panic for unrecoverable errors

content: Go functions returning (T, error) should always check err first before touching T, even if T looks like a safe zero value.
summary: Check Go error before using the value

content: Group multiple Go errors from a batch operation with errors.Join instead of only returning the first failure.
summary: Use errors.Join for batched Go errors

content: Log Go errors once at the boundary where they are handled, not at every layer they pass through, to avoid duplicate log spam.
summary: Log Go errors once at the handling boundary

content: Custom Go error types should implement Unwrap() error, not just Error() string, so they compose with errors.Is/As chains.
summary: Custom Go error types should implement Unwrap

content: When a Rust function only needs to read data, take a borrowed reference (&T) rather than taking ownership (T), so the caller keeps using the value afterward.
summary: Prefer borrowing over ownership in Rust when reading

content: Use Rc<RefCell<T>> in Rust only for single-threaded shared mutable state; reach for Arc<Mutex<T>> once the data crosses a thread boundary.
summary: Rc/RefCell vs Arc/Mutex in Rust

content: Clone in Rust is not free; profile before reaching for .clone() to silence a borrow checker error.
summary: Do not clone in Rust just to silence the borrow checker

content: Lifetime elision in Rust covers most function signatures; only annotate lifetimes explicitly when the compiler cannot infer them.
summary: Rely on Rust lifetime elision where possible

content: Prefer Rust iterators and combinators over manual index loops; the compiler optimizes iterator chains as well as hand-written loops.
summary: Prefer Rust iterator combinators over index loops

content: Unsafe Rust blocks must carry a comment explaining the invariant that makes them sound, per our internal style guide.
summary: Comment the invariant for every unsafe Rust block

content: Rust trait objects (dyn Trait) have runtime dispatch cost; prefer generics with trait bounds on hot paths.
summary: Prefer generics over dyn Trait on hot paths in Rust

content: useEffect cleanup functions in React must cancel in-flight requests or subscriptions, otherwise a fast-unmounting component leaks the effect.
summary: React useEffect must clean up in-flight work

content: Custom React hooks should always start with the word use and follow the rules of hooks (no conditional calls) so lint-plugin-react-hooks can check them.
summary: Naming and rules for custom React hooks

content: useMemo in React is for expensive recomputation, not for referential stability alone; useCallback is the right tool for stable function identity.
summary: useMemo vs useCallback in React

content: Avoid putting objects or arrays literal in a React useEffect dependency array; they create a new reference every render and cause infinite loops.
summary: Avoid literal objects in React effect deps

content: useReducer is preferred over multiple useState calls in React when state transitions are interrelated, e.g. a form with derived validation state.
summary: Prefer useReducer for interrelated React state

content: React context should not be used for high-frequency updates (like mouse position); it re-renders every consumer on every change.
summary: React context is a poor fit for high-frequency updates

content: Server components in React cannot use useState or useEffect; keep those in a nested client component boundary.
summary: React server components cannot use client-only hooks

content: Vue composables should return refs, not raw values, so callers keep reactivity when destructuring the composable result.
summary: Vue composables must return refs for reactivity

content: Use watchEffect in Vue when the dependency set is dynamic and derived automatically; use watch with an explicit source when you need the previous value.
summary: watchEffect vs watch in Vue composition API

content: Avoid deeply nested reactive() objects in Vue; prefer flatter state shapes so change detection stays cheap.
summary: Prefer flat reactive state shapes in Vue

content: Vue provide/inject should be typed with InjectionKey<T> so consumers get type safety instead of any.
summary: Type Vue provide/inject with InjectionKey

content: Script setup syntax in Vue 3 removes the need for a separate setup() return statement and is our default for new single-file components.
summary: Vue 3 script setup is the default SFC style

content: Vue computed properties must stay side-effect free; move any mutation into a watcher or method instead.
summary: Keep Vue computed properties side-effect free

content: Pinia stores replace Vuex for new Vue projects; define state as a function returning the initial object, not a plain object literal.
summary: Pinia replaces Vuex for new Vue projects

content: Use a multi-stage Dockerfile: build the app in a full SDK image, then copy only the compiled artifact into a slim runtime base image to shrink the final image size.
summary: Multi-stage Dockerfile keeps runtime images slim

content: Pin base images in Dockerfiles by digest (node:20-slim@sha256:...) for production builds, not just by tag, so a base image republish cannot silently change behavior.
summary: Pin Docker base images by digest for production

content: Order Dockerfile layers from least to most frequently changing (dependencies before source code) to maximize build cache reuse.
summary: Order Dockerfile layers for cache reuse

content: Run containers as a non-root user by default; add a USER directive near the end of the Dockerfile after installing dependencies as root.
summary: Docker containers should run as non-root

content: Use a .dockerignore file to exclude node_modules, .git, and test fixtures from the build context so builds stay fast.
summary: Use .dockerignore to keep Docker build context small

content: Health checks in Docker images (HEALTHCHECK instruction) should hit a lightweight internal endpoint, not the full readiness probe used by Kubernetes.
summary: Docker HEALTHCHECK should be lightweight

content: Avoid installing build-essential and other compiler toolchains in the final Docker image stage; keep them only in the builder stage.
summary: Keep compiler toolchains out of final Docker stage

content: Every Kubernetes deployment must set both resources.requests and resources.limits for CPU and memory; unset limits let one pod starve the node.
summary: Kubernetes pods must set resource requests and limits

content: Set Kubernetes memory limits equal to memory requests to avoid OOM-kill surprises from burstable QoS; only CPU is safe to leave burstable.
summary: Kubernetes memory limits should equal requests

content: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler in Kubernetes should target 60-70% CPU utilization, not 90%, to leave headroom for scale-up latency.
summary: Kubernetes HPA target CPU utilization

content: Use PodDisruptionBudgets in Kubernetes for any deployment that must stay available during node drains or cluster upgrades.
summary: Use PodDisruptionBudgets for availability during drains

content: Liveness probes in Kubernetes should never depend on downstream services; only readiness probes should.
summary: Kubernetes liveness probes must not depend on downstream services

content: Namespace-level ResourceQuotas in Kubernetes prevent one team from exhausting cluster capacity for everyone else.
summary: Use ResourceQuotas to cap namespace resource usage

content: Prefer Kubernetes Deployments over bare Pods for anything long-running, even single-replica services, for the built-in restart policy.
summary: Prefer Kubernetes Deployments over bare Pods

content: Add a PostgreSQL composite index matching the exact column order used in WHERE clauses; a mismatched column order makes the index unusable for that query.
summary: PostgreSQL composite index column order matters

content: Use a partial PostgreSQL index (CREATE INDEX ... WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) when most queries only ever touch active rows.
summary: Use partial PostgreSQL indexes for active-row queries

content: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on any PostgreSQL query before assuming an index will help; sequential scans can beat an index on small tables.
summary: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE before adding PostgreSQL indexes

content: GIN indexes in PostgreSQL are the right choice for JSONB containment queries and full-text search columns.
summary: Use GIN indexes for PostgreSQL JSONB and full-text search

content: Rebuild bloated PostgreSQL indexes with REINDEX CONCURRENTLY to avoid locking writes during the rebuild.
summary: Use REINDEX CONCURRENTLY for bloated PostgreSQL indexes

content: Too many PostgreSQL indexes slow down writes; audit unused indexes with pg_stat_user_indexes periodically.
summary: Audit unused PostgreSQL indexes with pg_stat_user_indexes

content: Foreign key columns in PostgreSQL are not automatically indexed; add the index explicitly or joins and cascading deletes will be slow.
summary: PostgreSQL foreign keys need explicit indexes

content: In MongoDB, embed data that is always read together and rarely updated independently; reference data that grows unboundedly or is shared across many parents.
summary: MongoDB embed-vs-reference rule of thumb

content: MongoDB documents should stay well under the 16MB limit in practice; anything approaching a few MB is a sign the schema needs to reference, not embed.
summary: Keep MongoDB documents well under the size limit

content: Use MongoDB schema validation (jsonSchema) on collections that accept writes from multiple services, so a bad write fails loudly.
summary: Use MongoDB schema validation for multi-writer collections

content: Compound indexes in MongoDB should follow the ESR rule: Equality fields, then Sort fields, then Range fields.
summary: MongoDB compound indexes follow the ESR rule

content: Avoid unbounded arrays inside a single MongoDB document; a growing array field is usually a sign it should be its own collection.
summary: Avoid unbounded arrays in a single MongoDB document

content: Use MongoDB change streams instead of polling when a downstream service needs near-real-time notification of writes.
summary: Use MongoDB change streams over polling

content: Shard MongoDB collections on a key with high cardinality and even write distribution, never on a monotonically increasing field alone.
summary: Choose a high-cardinality MongoDB shard key

content: Set a Redis TTL on every cache key by default; a cache without expiry silently turns into a second source of truth that drifts from the database.
summary: Every Redis cache key needs a default TTL

content: Use Redis cache-aside (lazy loading) for read-heavy, write-light data; use write-through caching only when staleness is unacceptable.
summary: Redis cache-aside vs write-through caching

content: Avoid the Redis KEYS command in production; use SCAN with a cursor to iterate keys without blocking the event loop.
summary: Use Redis SCAN instead of KEYS in production

content: Namespace Redis keys with a colon-delimited prefix (service:entity:id) so different services never collide in a shared cluster.
summary: Namespace Redis keys by service and entity

content: Use Redis Pub/Sub for fire-and-forget notifications, not for anything that needs delivery guarantees; a stream or queue is the right tool for that.
summary: Redis Pub/Sub has no delivery guarantees

content: Pick eviction policy allkeys-lru for a pure cache Redis instance, and noeviction for a Redis instance used as a durable queue or store.
summary: Pick Redis eviction policy based on use case

content: Cache stampedes against Redis are mitigated with a short jittered TTL or a single-flight lock around the recompute.
summary: Mitigate Redis cache stampedes with jitter or single-flight

content: Schema stitching combines multiple GraphQL schemas at the gateway; federation instead lets each subgraph own its types and the gateway composes them at build time.
summary: GraphQL schema stitching vs federation

content: GraphQL resolvers should never trigger N+1 database queries; use DataLoader to batch and cache per-request lookups.
summary: Use DataLoader to avoid GraphQL N+1 queries

content: Version GraphQL schemas by deprecating fields with @deprecated and a reason, never by breaking existing queries outright.
summary: Deprecate GraphQL fields instead of breaking changes

content: Depth-limit and complexity-limit incoming GraphQL queries to prevent a single malicious or buggy client from overloading the server.
summary: Depth and complexity limit incoming GraphQL queries

content: Use GraphQL input types, not loose scalar arguments, for any mutation taking more than two or three fields.
summary: Use GraphQL input types for multi-field mutations

content: Persisted queries reduce GraphQL request payload size and let the server allow-list exactly which queries clients can run.
summary: GraphQL persisted queries reduce payload and allow-list queries

content: GraphQL subscriptions should be reserved for genuinely real-time data; polling a query is simpler and fine for anything under a few seconds of staleness.
summary: Reserve GraphQL subscriptions for genuinely real-time data

content: Version REST APIs in the URL path (/v1/, /v2/) rather than a custom header, so the version is visible in logs and easy for clients to pin.
summary: Version REST APIs in the URL path

content: Never remove a field from a REST API response in a minor version; only additive changes are allowed without bumping the major version.
summary: REST API minor versions must be additive only

content: REST endpoints should return 429 with a Retry-After header when rate limiting a client, not a bare 403.
summary: REST rate limiting should return 429 with Retry-After

content: Use PATCH with a JSON Merge Patch or JSON Patch body for partial REST updates, not a full-resource PUT for a one-field change.
summary: Use PATCH for partial REST updates

content: Pagination on REST list endpoints should use an opaque cursor, not raw offset/limit, so results stay stable while the underlying data changes.
summary: Use cursor pagination on REST list endpoints

content: REST error responses should follow a single consistent envelope shape across every endpoint, including the error code and a human-readable message.
summary: Use a consistent REST error response envelope

content: Idempotency keys are required on REST POST endpoints that create billing or payment records, to survive client retries safely.
summary: Require idempotency keys on REST payment POST endpoints

content: Jest test files should co-locate with the source file (foo.ts + foo.test.ts) rather than living in a separate top-level tests directory, so they move together during refactors.
summary: Co-locate Jest test files with source

content: Mock only the boundary a Jest unit test actually needs (network, filesystem, clock); mocking internal collaborators too aggressively makes the test assert its own mocks.
summary: Mock boundaries, not internal collaborators, in Jest tests

content: Use Jest fake timers (jest.useFakeTimers) for anything testing debounce, throttle, or setTimeout-driven retry logic.
summary: Use Jest fake timers for time-driven logic

content: Snapshot tests in Jest are appropriate for stable serialized output, not for UI components that change frequently and get blindly re-approved.
summary: Use Jest snapshots only for stable output

content: Every Jest describe block should share one behavior under test; splitting unrelated assertions into the same block makes failures hard to read.
summary: Keep one Jest describe block per behavior

content: Reset Jest mocks between tests with clearMocks in config rather than manual afterEach boilerplate in every file.
summary: Reset Jest mocks via clearMocks config, not manual afterEach

content: Coverage thresholds in Jest should gate CI on statements and branches, not just line coverage, to catch untested conditional paths.
summary: Gate Jest coverage on branches, not just lines

content: Pytest fixtures with database setup should use function scope by default; only widen to session scope once you have proven test isolation is not needed.
summary: Pytest fixture scope defaults to function-level

content: Parametrize pytest tests with @pytest.mark.parametrize instead of writing a loop inside a single test function, so each case reports independently.
summary: Use pytest.mark.parametrize instead of loops in tests

content: Use pytest conftest.py fixtures for cross-cutting setup shared by a whole directory, not by importing helper functions into every test file.
summary: Use pytest conftest.py for shared fixtures

content: Mark slow or integration pytest tests with a custom marker and exclude them from the fast default test run via pytest.ini.
summary: Mark and exclude slow pytest tests by default

content: Prefer pytest monkeypatch over unittest.mock.patch for simple attribute/env var overrides; it auto-reverts and needs less boilerplate.
summary: Prefer pytest monkeypatch for simple overrides

content: Assert pytest exceptions with pytest.raises as a context manager, and check the message with match= rather than a bare except in the test.
summary: Use pytest.raises with match for exception tests

content: Factory fixtures in pytest (fixtures that return a function) are the right pattern when a test needs several differently-configured instances.
summary: Use pytest factory fixtures for multiple configured instances

content: GitHub Actions workflows should cache npm/pip dependencies with actions/cache keyed on the lockfile hash, not on a fixed key, so a dependency bump invalidates the cache correctly.
summary: GitHub Actions cache keyed on lockfile hash

content: Split GitHub Actions CI into separate lint, test, and build jobs that run in parallel rather than one long sequential job, to shorten feedback time.
summary: Run GitHub Actions lint/test/build jobs in parallel

content: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA, not a floating tag like @v3, to avoid a supply-chain surprise from an upstream Action update.
summary: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA

content: Use GitHub Actions matrix builds to test against multiple Node/Python versions in one workflow definition instead of duplicating jobs.
summary: Use GitHub Actions matrix builds for multi-version testing

content: Secrets in GitHub Actions should be scoped to the minimum required environment, not exposed to every job in the workflow.
summary: Scope GitHub Actions secrets to the minimum environment

content: Fail GitHub Actions workflows fast with fail-fast: true on matrix builds during development, but disable it before a release branch build.
summary: Use fail-fast appropriately on GitHub Actions matrices

content: Upload GitHub Actions build artifacts with a short retention period for PR builds and a longer one for main branch builds.
summary: Set retention period for GitHub Actions artifacts

content: Jenkins deployment pipelines should be defined as a Jenkinsfile checked into the repo, not configured through the classic web UI, so pipeline changes go through code review.
summary: Jenkins pipelines defined as code, not UI config

content: Jenkins deployment stages should require manual approval before promoting to production, but can auto-promote through staging.
summary: Jenkins requires manual approval before production deploy

content: Store Jenkins credentials in the built-in credentials store, never as plaintext environment variables in a Jenkinsfile.
summary: Store Jenkins credentials in the credentials store

content: Use Jenkins shared libraries to de-duplicate common pipeline steps across repositories instead of copy-pasting Jenkinsfile stages.
summary: Use Jenkins shared libraries to de-duplicate pipeline steps

content: Archive Jenkins build logs and test reports as artifacts so a failed deployment can be diagnosed after the agent is recycled.
summary: Archive Jenkins build logs and test reports

content: Jenkins agents used for deployment should be ephemeral (spun up per build) rather than long-lived, to avoid state drift between runs.
summary: Use ephemeral Jenkins agents for deployment

content: Rollback in the Jenkins deployment pipeline should redeploy the previous known-good artifact, not attempt to revert code and rebuild under pressure.
summary: Jenkins rollback redeploys the previous known-good artifact

content: We use trunk-based development with short-lived feature branches merged via squash-merge, not long-running gitflow release branches.
summary: Trunk-based development with squash-merge feature branches

content: Never force-push to main or a shared branch; force-push is only acceptable on a personal feature branch after a rebase.
summary: Never force-push to main or shared branches

content: Delete a git branch immediately after it is merged; stale branches accumulate and make `git branch` noise for everyone.
summary: Delete git branches immediately after merge

content: Rebase feature branches onto main before opening a PR, but never rebase a branch other people have already pulled.
summary: Rebase before opening a PR, never rebase shared history

content: Git commit messages should follow conventional commits (feat:, fix:, chore:) so changelogs can be generated automatically.
summary: Use conventional commits for git commit messages

content: Protect the main git branch with required status checks and at least one required review before merge is allowed.
summary: Protect main git branch with required checks and review

content: Tag git releases with semantic version tags (v1.4.0) immediately after the release branch merges to main.
summary: Tag git releases with semantic version numbers

content: Code review comments should distinguish blocking issues from optional nits, e.g. by prefixing nits with "nit:" so authors know what must be fixed before merge.
summary: Distinguish blocking code review comments from nits

content: A pull request should have a single clear purpose; reviewers can ask the author to split an unrelated change into a separate PR.
summary: Keep each pull request to a single clear purpose

content: Code review turnaround target is one business day; a PR sitting longer than that should be pinged in the team channel.
summary: Target one business day for code review turnaround

content: Reviewers should pull down and run a PR locally for anything touching data migrations, not just read the diff.
summary: Run migration PRs locally, do not just read the diff

content: Approve a code review with a comment explaining what you checked, not a bare thumbs-up, so future readers understand the review depth.
summary: Explain what was checked when approving a code review

content: Large refactor PRs should be reviewed commit-by-commit rather than as one giant diff, when the author split the work into logical commits.
summary: Review large refactors commit-by-commit

content: Author self-review (reading your own diff before requesting review) catches a large share of avoidable review comments.
summary: Self-review your diff before requesting review

content: We decided against splitting the billing module into a separate microservice this quarter; the team is too small to carry the added operational overhead yet.
summary: Decision: billing stays in the monolith this quarter

content: The notifications module was split out into its own service because its scaling profile (bursty, high-volume) was fundamentally different from the rest of the monolith.
summary: Decision: notifications split out due to different scaling profile

content: Extracting a service should be justified by an independent scaling, deployment, or team-ownership need, not by architectural taste alone.
summary: Service extraction needs a concrete justification

content: Every new microservice adds an on-call rotation burden; we track that cost explicitly before approving a split.
summary: New microservices add on-call burden to weigh

content: We prefer a modular monolith with clear internal module boundaries over premature microservices for a team our size.
summary: Prefer a modular monolith at our current team size

content: Shared database access across services was explicitly ruled out; each service that does get split owns its own datastore.
summary: No shared database access across split services

content: A service boundary is easier to draw along a bounded context from domain modeling than along an org chart line.
summary: Draw service boundaries along bounded contexts

content: Use an event-driven architecture with a message queue for workflows that can tolerate eventual consistency; keep synchronous request/response for anything the caller needs to confirm immediately.
summary: Event-driven messaging for eventually-consistent workflows

content: Every published event on our message queue must be versioned and backward compatible for at least one deprecation cycle before a breaking change ships.
summary: Published events must stay backward compatible

content: Consumers of our message queue must be idempotent, because at-least-once delivery means a message can be redelivered.
summary: Message queue consumers must be idempotent

content: Use a dead-letter queue for messages that fail processing repeatedly, rather than dropping them or retrying forever.
summary: Use a dead-letter queue for repeatedly failing messages

content: Event payloads should carry enough context to be processed independently; avoid forcing consumers to call back to the producer for details.
summary: Event payloads should be self-contained

content: Choose a message broker based on delivery and ordering guarantees you actually need, not on popularity alone.
summary: Choose a message broker based on actual delivery needs

content: Trace correlation IDs must propagate through every hop of an event-driven workflow so a failure can be followed end to end.
summary: Propagate correlation IDs through event-driven workflows

content: We adopted CQRS for the reporting module only, keeping a separate read model updated asynchronously from the write model, because reporting queries were degrading write-path latency.
summary: Decision: CQRS adopted for reporting module only

content: CQRS was explicitly rejected for the core order-processing module; the added complexity was not justified by its read/write load profile.
summary: Decision: CQRS rejected for order-processing module

content: A CQRS read model can lag the write model; any UI relying on it must communicate eventual consistency to the user.
summary: CQRS read models can lag and must communicate that

content: CQRS is not a prerequisite for event sourcing, and we are not adopting event sourcing alongside it at this time.
summary: CQRS adopted without event sourcing

content: Command handlers in our CQRS module validate business rules; the read side never performs validation, only projection.
summary: CQRS command handlers own validation, not the read side

content: Rebuilding a CQRS read model from the event log must be possible from scratch, as a disaster-recovery guarantee.
summary: CQRS read models must be rebuildable from scratch

content: We revisit the CQRS decision for a module whenever its read and write load profiles diverge significantly, not on a fixed schedule.
summary: Revisit CQRS decisions when load profiles diverge

content: Access JWTs are short-lived (15 minutes) and refresh tokens are long-lived but rotated on every use, so a stolen refresh token is detectable via reuse.
summary: Short-lived access JWTs, rotated refresh tokens

content: JWTs are never used to carry authorization decisions directly; the token only proves identity, and permission checks always hit the authorization service.
summary: JWTs prove identity only, not authorization

content: Validate JWT signature, issuer, audience, and expiry on every request; never trust a decoded-but-unverified payload.
summary: Fully validate JWTs on every request

content: Store JWTs in an httpOnly, Secure cookie for browser clients, never in localStorage, to reduce XSS token theft risk.
summary: Store browser JWTs in httpOnly cookies, not localStorage

content: Rotate the JWT signing key on a schedule and support two active keys during the rotation window via a key ID (kid) header.
summary: Rotate JWT signing keys with overlapping validity

content: JWT claims should be minimal; do not embed a user's full profile in the token just to avoid a database lookup.
summary: Keep JWT claims minimal

content: Revoking a single compromised JWT before its expiry requires a deny-list check, which is why access token lifetime is kept short.
summary: Short JWT lifetime avoids needing a deny-list for revocation

content: All customer PII at rest is encrypted with AES-256, with keys managed by the cloud KMS, never hardcoded or checked into the repo.
summary: PII at rest encrypted with AES-256 via cloud KMS

content: Database backups inherit the same at-rest encryption as the primary database; an unencrypted backup would undermine the whole policy.
summary: Database backups must inherit at-rest encryption

content: Encryption keys are rotated annually at minimum, and immediately after any suspected key compromise.
summary: Encryption keys rotated at least annually

content: Field-level encryption is applied to the most sensitive columns (SSNs, payment tokens) in addition to whole-disk encryption.
summary: Field-level encryption on the most sensitive columns

content: Access to decryption keys is logged and alerts on any access outside the expected service accounts.
summary: Decryption key access is logged and alerted on

content: Data in transit between internal services uses mTLS, which is a separate control from at-rest encryption but equally required.
summary: Internal service traffic uses mTLS in addition to at-rest encryption

content: Encryption at rest does not replace access control; both are required layers per our security policy.
summary: Encryption at rest is not a substitute for access control

content: The engineering team moved standup from daily to three times a week after feedback that daily standups were mostly status theater for a team this small.
summary: Standup reduced from daily to three times a week

content: Sprint planning happens every other Monday and is capped at 60 minutes; anything needing more discussion gets a separate follow-up.
summary: Sprint planning is biweekly, capped at 60 minutes

content: Retro is held at the end of every sprint and always ends with at most three concrete action items, not an open-ended list.
summary: Retro caps action items at three per sprint

content: One-on-ones between engineers and their manager are scheduled weekly by default, but can drop to biweekly if both sides agree.
summary: One-on-ones default weekly, can drop to biweekly

content: Meetings without a written agenda sent in advance are discouraged; the team can decline to attend an agenda-less meeting.
summary: Meetings need a written agenda sent in advance

content: All-hands meetings are recorded and posted with notes for anyone in a different timezone who could not attend live.
summary: All-hands meetings are recorded for other timezones

content: Design review meetings are scheduled only once a written design doc exists; there is no design review of a verbal idea alone.
summary: Design review requires a written doc first
